Home » Welcome to Cricklade Manor Prep » Extra-Curricular Success
As a school we place an equal emphasis on non-academic successes as well as academics. We recognise that all children have different strengths and passions and the importance of celebrating all of these.
Our students actively participated in 28 different sports club outside of school, including Cricket, Rugby, Football, Netball, Hockey, Athletics, Swimming, Gymnastics, and Tennis. Notably, 4 of our children represent County Cricket teams, one excels as a Regional Gymnast, and another as a County Tennis player.
Public speaking is an integral part of our curriculum, and 13 children receive LAMDA lessons, where they sit exams in various aspects, including Prose and Poetry, Acting, and Mime.
Our Music room, a converted Chapel with exceptional acoustics, serves as an inspirational space. Currently, 57 children are taking individual piano lessons, 3 are enrolled in Violin lessons, and 12 are passionate about playing the Drums. The number of students taking ABRSM exams is on the rise, with 13 successfully passing exams last year.

Home » Welcome to Cricklade Manor Prep » Equality, Diversity and Inclusion
Cricklade Manor Prep is a diverse family focused school in which all children are celebrated, feel valued and included. Pupils of all faiths, religious beliefs and backgrounds, are encouraged to confidently share their family heritage to inform their fellow pupils. Our comprehensive and inclusive curriculum is enhanced by our school’s multicultural and diverse community.
Watch our wonderful video created by our students embracing the diversity within our school.
Pupils had the fantastic opportunity to participate and experience a wide range of faiths as part of our Interfaith Week, shared with our parental community.
Watch the video below to see how the whole school came together to embrace this enriching experience.
“Thank you so much for creating a space where we could share our beliefs and foster understanding among young minds and with teachers. Personally experiencing diverse faiths under one roof for the first time was truly extraordinary for me.”
The formation of our EDI committee has allowed us to raise the profile of our EDI within Cricklade Manor Prep, increasing knowledge, respect and understanding of each individual.

Home » Welcome to Cricklade Manor Prep » Inspection Reports
In June 2024, Cricklade Manor Prep was inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate, the independent schools equivalent to Ofsted. Our first full inspection for seven years, it was a very positive experience, and we are delighted with the inspectors’ findings.
The inspectors have praised many aspects of our school, but best of all, they awarded us a Significant Strength. These are a rare – with only a handful of schools across the country receiving such an accolade. It recognises a particular strength of provision that has a clear, demonstrable and highly beneficial impact for pupils.
The Cricklade Pupil Development (CPD) programme provides every pupil with a programme to support areas of relative weakness and to provide greater depth in areas of strength. Its impact on pupils’ attainment over time is clear and measurable. The programme is a significant strength of the school.

Home » Welcome to Cricklade Manor Prep » Year 6 Leavers
By the time a child leaves Cricklade Manor Prep, our intention is that each child has discovered their talents, experienced success and is able to move onwards with strong self-esteem and a personal belief in what they can achieve.
Our children go onto a range of excellent grammar, independent and state senior schools, including fellow Wishford school, Westonbirt School. For those children taking entrance exams, we have a programme of support to help them prepare.
In recent years, children have moved on to schools including Malmesbury School, Dean Close School, Dauntsey’s School, Pate’s Grammar School, and Stroud High Grammar School.
11+ Success 2026
We are proud to announce that 13 out of 16 of our Year 6 children who sat the 11+ exams were successful, of whom 9 chose to join the grammar schools Stroud High, Sir Thomas Rich, Ribston Hall, Marling and Pates Grammar School this year. Our children were also awarded the following scholarships:
1 – Academic to Kingswood, Bath (accepted)
3 – Sport to Westonbirt School (two accepted, one declined)
1 – Academic to Westonbirt School (accepted)
1 – Headmasters Award to Dean Close (declined)
1 – Academic and Sport to Christ’s Hospital (declined)
1 – Sports Development Pathway to Westonbirt (accepted)
Summer 2026 Leavers
Other destination schools this year include Westonbirt School, Hatherop Castle, St Johns, Kingshill School, Farmors, Dauntsey’s and Great Western Academy.
We are incredibly proud of all our Leavers who achieved so much in their time with us. We know that the leadership, communication, and collaboration skills they have developed with us will serve them well in their secondary schools.
For a full list of the destinations of last year’s leavers, click here.
Summer 2026 Year 6 Attainment
To support the children’s progress, it is very important that we can assess them regularly to ensure we are supporting and challenging each individual child. As an independent school we are not restricted by the SATS but feel it is very important we have an accurate understanding of each child’s progress. We assess the children in Maths and English termly, which provides us with nationally recognised standardised scores in these areas.
As a non-selective school we are enormously proud of the achievements of our Y6 pupils. 96% of our Year 6 Leavers were ‘working at’ or ‘exceeding expectations’ in Maths. Similarly, over 91% of our Year 6 leavers were ‘working at’ or ‘exceeding expectations’ in the core area of English.

pageCache.text:
Home » Welcome to Cricklade Manor Prep » Facilities
Cricklade Manor Prep has outstanding facilities for a school of its size. The old Manor House and its surrounding buildings provide light and spacious learning spaces, while beyond, invisible from the road, 8 acres of grounds take in play areas and sports fields.
Science laboratories
We talk a lot at Cricklade Manor about helping our children develop a love of learning. A perfect example would be the impact of our science laboratories on pupils’ attitudes to this core academic subject. Having access to fully equipped labs dramatically enhances their experience of science. There are opportunities for children of all ages to take part in practical experiments, bringing science to life, sparking a passion for and a deeper understanding of physics, chemistry and biology. Pupils learn practical scientific skills and principles, as well as the responsible handling of chemicals, Bunsen burners and other key pieces of scientific equipment, which will put them at an advantage in senior school.
Sports facilities
Sport is key to life at Cricklade Manor Prep, building gross motor skills, teamwork, strategic thinking, fitness and mental wellbeing. As well as plenty of time built into the curriculum, our pupils have access to high quality sport facilities in all weathers.
The full-sized sports hall is equipped for very wide range of sports, from gymnastics and netball, to indoor cricket and fencing.
Outside, are two full-sized grass pitches for rugby, football and cricket, as well as astro pitches for hockey and netball, and two hard tennis courts.
Our outdoor swimming pool is used throughout summer by children from Nursery upwards, and has supported the development of a number of outstanding county swimmers.
Lego robotics
In an increasingly technological world, developing a thorough grounding in information technology is vital. As at most schools, children here have access to computers, and learn a range of IT skills, but it is the Lego robotics which really makes a difference to their grasp of technology and its application in a wider context. Within our tech curriculum, children from Year 3 use Lego robotics, programmable robotic kits using computer elements, bricks, modular sensors and motors. As well as the enormous fun and sense of achievement children get from creating and controlling their own machines, Lego robotics builds skills in problem solving, design, engineering and coding. Children can challenge each other, and take part in external competitions too.
Forest School
The beautiful Forest School area is dedicated to outdoor learning. Time there is special, giving our children space and freedom. There are countless ways outdoor learning can support the academic curriculum, from maths and science to art and English, but crucially it helps pupils develop a deeper understanding of and respect for the natural world, underlining the key principle that we have to work within the Earth’s resources.
Art
Step into the school office and the incredible displays on the walls reveal the standard of art at Cricklade Manor Prep. We are incredibly proud of our Art Department and the opportunities it provides to our pupils to explore their creativity and develop skills across a wide range of visual arts, from painting and pastels to batik and ceramics, fired in our own kiln. As well as the smaller, individual pieces of work, there is scope for the children to create on much bigger scale, including the enormous art installations displayed in the atrium outside the main hall each term.

Home » Welcome to Cricklade Manor Prep » Moving to North Wiltshire & The Cotswolds
The historic Saxon town of Cricklade is the Southern gateway to the Cotswolds. Moving to this area is the ultimate dream for many, a naturally popular choice for people who want to enjoy a rural lifestyle without losing touch with the shopping and cultural activities associated with city living.
Cricklade Manor Prep School sits midway between Swindon and Cirencester. It is within easy reach of the vibrant, historic cities of Bath, Oxford and Cheltenham.
Transport links
The M4 motorway and fast-speed rail links (from Swindon, Kemble or Oxford Parkway) allow a rapid commute to London. Bristol airport is convenient for travel throughout Europe, and Heathrow is just over an hour away. It is also well placed for access to other popular destinations: Devon and Cornwall are just down the M5. The stunning Gower Peninsula on the south coast of Wales is another holiday hotspot within easy each, and the M5/M6 route makes travel to the North straightforward.
Property
This area is filled with extraordinarily picturesque villages, with beautiful houses built in the characteristic honey-coloured Cotswold stone. From quaint cottages to large country houses, the traditional architecture of this part of the world alone is a huge draw, and many properties have extensive gardens and grounds.
Local estate agents include Savills, Knight Frank and Strutt & Parker. Click on the link to see houses currently for sale in the area: Houses for sale.
Shopping
Moving to North Wiltshire or the Cotswolds doesn’t mean leaving civilisation behind! Cirencester, Cheltenham and Gloucester are all within easy reach of Cricklade for shopping. Bristol is also less than an hour away. The Swindon Outlet Centre and Bath’s South Gate are popular high street brand shopping destinations. Whilst independent retailers like Indico and Sam Venn Interiors are right on Cricklade’s own high street. In fact, independent and local produce is aplenty in this area. You can get some fantastic finds at the regular weekend markets in Cirencester, Marlborough and Stroud, boasting wonderful locally sourced produce and gifts.
Eating
From cosying up by the log fire in a traditional country pub like the The Red Lion in Castle Eaton, to taking a family stroll along the water in South Cerney to get their highly rated fish and chips, there’s a café, pub or restaurant to everyone’s taste here. Including some high class eateries – Conde Nast Traveller gives their picks here, citing the Cotswolds as the ‘foodiest patch outside London’.
Family days out
Amongst the glorious countryside there are a number of local attractions that are sure to keep the kids entertained at the weekend. The Cotswold Water Park, covering 40 square miles, is a series of more than 150 lakes. As well as being an important wildlife area, it provides a wide range of water sports, from sailing and kayaking to fishing and paddle boarding.
Cycling is another popular family sport around here, with lots of off-road routes to explore in the area. Stanton Country Park and The Ridgeway (often described as Britain’s oldest road) are popular routes amongst Cricklade Manor Prep families.
The Cotswold Wildlife Park is an exciting day out for little ones and older ones alike. They schedule a number of fun and educational events throughout the year. The Swindon STEAM Museum is another great day out that schedules educational events throughout the year.
Stately homes, grounds and National Trust properties are also in abundance here. Popular among Cricklade Manor Prep families to visit include Bowood House, Westonbirt Arboretum and Lacock.
Arts & Culture
Theatre buffs are well served by the Wyvern Theatre in Swindon, Cheltenham’s Everyman Theatre, the highly regarded Theatre Royal in Bath and Cirencester’s Barn Theatre. A little further afield in Bristol, the Hippodrome hosts all the best shows from London’s West End.
O2 Bristol is a great music venue, as is Colston Hall. For a more rural vibe, Westonbirt Arboretum hosts extremely popular outdoor concerts every summer.
Both the Holbourne Museum and Victoria Art Gallery in Bath offer a consistent stream of interesting collections and exhibits to explore.
The Cricklade Manor Prep Community
Our strong Cricklade Manor Prep community offers a supportive and welcoming network. If you have any questions about moving to this beautiful area, or would like advice on places to live, please let us know, and we’ll do our best to help.

Welcome to Subject Spotlight: Inspiring Young Minds. In this series, we take the opportunity to shine the light on the incredible subjects and specialist teachers that make Cricklade Manor Prep’s creative curriculum so enriching. Hear from our wonderful staff, who shape Cricklade Manor Prep’s excellence; why they are so passionate about their subject and why they think it is so important for children to study.
ENGLISH & DRAMA: Miss Blissett
1) Why do you love English & Drama?
I didn’t always love reading. For a long time, books felt just… fine. But then, I found the book—the one that pulled me in, made the characters feel real, and turned reading into an experience. That story changed everything, and soon, I couldn’t stop. Now, I love English because I know there’s a book out there for everyone—one that can spark their imagination and make them fall in love with reading, just like I did. That’s why I’m passionate about ensuring every classroom library is packed with engaging books, so every student has the chance to find their book!
As for drama, I’ve always enjoyed the subject, but what really excites me is seeing how it can develop a student’s confidence once that spark is noticed. It’s incredible to watch a pupil, who might have been quiet or unsure at first, fully embrace a role and step into their character with newfound confidence. Drama isn’t just about performance—it’s about giving every student the opportunity to discover their voice, push their limits, and realise that they have something valuable to offer, both on and off the stage. Whether it be rewording the script, a way someone should react or creating choreography. Drama is a space where every child can explore, grow, and enjoy being part of something huge!
2) Why do you think English & Drama are important subjects to learn?
English is EVERYWHERE! It’s not just about books and essays—it’s how we express our thoughts, persuade others, make sense of the world, and share ideas. Imagine trying to tell a joke without the right words or persuading your parents to get a pet dragon (or just a later bedtime!) without using a well-crafted argument. Good communication opens doors—to friendships, careers, and new opportunities. Plus, being able to read critically and write effectively means you can navigate the world with confidence, whether that’s understanding a news article, crafting a brilliant email, or delivering an Oscar-worthy speech!
3) What benefits do you think children gain from studying English and Drama?
First, confidence—whether it’s mastering a speech, performing a poem, or stepping into a character through drama, English helps pupils find their voice and believe in themselves. Then, creativity—it encourages them to think outside the box, invent new worlds, and explore different perspectives, both on the page and on the stage. It also builds empathy—reading and performing stories allow pupils to step into other people’s shoes and truly understand different experiences. And let’s not forget critical thinking—analysing texts, crafting arguments, and interpreting characters help pupils think deeply and become independent thinkers. Whether they’re writing, reading, speaking, or performing, English shapes them into articulate, thoughtful, and creative individuals ready to take on the world!
4) What do you enjoy most about being a teacher at Cricklade Manor Prep?
Cricklade Manor Prep is bursting with energy, creativity, and a team of dedicated teachers who aren’t afraid to take risks in their teaching. They trust the process, embrace new ideas, and because of that, the children reap the rewards—becoming curious, confident, and engaged learners. The pupils’ enthusiasm is infectious, making every lesson an adventure!
But for me, the real magic is in bringing stories to life through drama. With close links between drama and English, I love seeing pupils step into roles, explore characters, and transform words into something unforgettable. Drama isn’t just acting—it’s about confidence, creativity, and making stories jump off the page. And there’s no better place to do it than here!
5) How do you think Cricklade Manor Prep sets us apart from other schools and makes us truly exceptional?
At Cricklade Manor Prep, we thoughtfully bring selected English topics to life through immersive, hands-on experiences that inspire awe and wonder in every child. This purposeful approach ignites imaginations and fosters a love for storytelling and creative expression. From undertaking a daring initiation test inspired by How to Train Your Dragon, reenacting the task of washing a woolly mammoth, uncovering secrets hidden within a mysterious suitcase, or venturing into the depths of an Egyptian tomb to craft evocative descriptive writing, our students are immersed in a world of discovery. These carefully designed experiential learning opportunities set our school apart, ensuring that English is not just studied but truly lived, sparking enthusiasm and creativity in meaningful ways.
1) Why do you love Maths?
As a Maths lead, I love Maths because it is both beautifully logical and endlessly creative. My love for Maths began as a child, when I would spend hours with a simple puzzle book that my parents gave me. I remember sitting by the window on rainy afternoons, captivated by the joy of cracking codes and solving number riddles. One specific moment stands out: I solved a particularly tricky puzzle that had stumped me for days, and the sense of achievement was unparalleled. That early spark ignited a lifelong passion for the subject, and I’ve carried that same curiosity and sense of discovery into my teaching. Maths provides a universal
language to solve problems, explore patterns, and make sense of the world around us. It’s not just about numbers but about critical thinking and discovery, which keeps me inspired every day.
2) Why do you think Maths is an important subject to learn?
Maths is foundational to understanding and thriving in today’s world. It develops essential problem-solving skills, logical reasoning, and the ability to make data-driven decisions. From budgeting and technology to architecture and medicine, Maths underpins countless aspects of modern life. Beyond practicality, it teaches resilience and a structured way to approach complex challenges, preparing pupils for future academic, professional, and personal success.
3) What benefits do you think children gain from studying Maths?
Studying Maths equips pupils with critical thinking and analytical skills, empowering them to tackle problems with confidence and persistence. It sharpens their ability to reason, interpret data, and recognise patterns. Additionally, Maths fosters creativity and curiosity, encouraging students to think outside the box. It also builds a growth mindset, teaching children that effort and practice lead to improvement, which is a valuable lesson for life.
4) What do you enjoy most about being a teacher at Cricklade Manor Prep?
Being a teacher at Cricklade Manor Prep is a joy because of the strong sense of community and the opportunity to nurture each pupil’s unique potential. The small class sizes allow for a more tailored and supportive approach to teaching, ensuring every child feels seen and valued. I especially appreciate the school’s emphasis on fostering a love for learning and curiosity, which aligns perfectly with my passion for Maths.
5) How do you think Cricklade Manor Prep sets us apart from other schools and makes us truly exceptional?
Cricklade Manor Prep stands out because of its holistic approach to education. The school prioritises academic excellence while also emphasising personal growth, creativity, and character development. The nurturing environment, dedicated staff, and close-knit community ensure that pupils feel supported and inspired to achieve their best. Our innovative teaching methods, enriched curriculum, and focus on each child as an individual truly make us exceptional, preparing students not just for exams but for life.
1) Why do you love Science?
I love Science because there’s always something new to discover! Every experiment and discovery the pupils make in my lab feels like they’re unlocking a new mystery. It’s thrilling to see the excitement in their eyes when they witness something amazing or make connections for the first time. Whether it’s Year 6 growing mould, Year 3 investigating fossils, or our Nursery children going on a bug hunt, the joy that comes from these lessons is the part I love the most.
2) Why do you think Science is an important subject to learn?
Science is crucial because it helps us understand the world around us.
It teaches us to think critically, ask questions, and solve problems. Plus, it’s the foundation for so many incredible careers and innovations that shape our future.
3) What benefits do you think children gain from studying Science?
Pupils gain so much from studying Science! They develop curiosity, creativity, and a love for learning. They also learn valuable skills like observation, experimentation, and logical thinking, which are useful in everyday life and any career they choose. But most importantly they learn to ask…Why?
4) What do you enjoy most about being a teacher at Cricklade Manor Prep?
What I enjoy most is the positive and supportive environment we have here. It’s wonderful to see pupils discovering things for themselves and developing a deep love for learning.
5) How do you think Cricklade Manor Prep sets us apart from other schools and makes us truly exceptional?
Cricklade Manor Prep is exceptional because we focus on nurturing each child’s individual strengths and interests. Our hands-on, engaging approach to teaching, especially in Science, helps pupils develop a genuine passion for discovery and self-learning. The supportive community here makes every pupil feel valued and inspired to reach their full potential.
DIRECTOR OF PASTORAL CARE: Mr Barton
1) What do you love about your role, being Director of Pastoral Care?
I truly cherish the opportunity to build meaningful relationships with my pupils outside of the classroom. These connections allow me to understand their individual needs and strengths, which ultimately helps them thrive academically and emotionally. I hope my presence creates a safe space where they feel valued and understood, enabling them to flourish not just as students but as individuals.
2) Why do you think it is important for children to learn about pastoral care in school?
It’s vital for children to see the school as a
nurturing environment that extends beyond academics. Learning about pastoral care helps them recognise that emotional and social well-being is just as important as their studies. This understanding fosters resilience, empathy, and the ability to seek help when needed, equipping them with essential life skills.
3) What benefits do you think children gain from studying issues regarding pastoral care?
Engaging with pastoral care issues encourages children to develop emotional intelligence, helping them navigate their feelings and those of others. It promotes open dialogue about mental health, builds a sense of community, and empowers them to be advocates for themselves and their peers. Ultimately, these discussions help create a culture of kindness and understanding within the school.
4) What do you enjoy most about being a teacher at Cricklade Manor Prep?
What I enjoy most is the sense of community and the strong connections I form with both students and staff. There’s a genuine commitment to nurturing the whole child here and witnessing the growth and happiness of my students is incredibly rewarding. Each day brings new opportunities to inspire and be inspired!

Home » Welcome to Cricklade Manor Prep » Why choose us?
Cricklade Manor Prep is a strongly performing school that supports and challenges children to achieve their potential.
With a broad and exciting curriculum, strength in the core subjects, countless extra-curricular opportunities, and excellent facilities, we are a supportive and welcoming community of children, staff and parents.
Individual attention in small classes
Our class sizes are small, and we have no combined age groups, which allows teachers to give every child the support he or she needs, with no danger of anyone slipping under the radar in a busy classroom.
This focus on each and every child extends into the Individual Learning Sessions which are built into the school week. In these, pupils have the option to receive a bit of extra support where needed, to spend more time on topics they love, or to try out something entirely new.
The same attention is brought to children’s emotional and mental wellbeing. Happy children are better learners, so there is plenty of time for imaginative play, sport, confidence building and friendships. Risk taking and learning to fail form a key part of learning from an early age, ensuring that our older children take on challenges with a healthy combination of positivity and resilience.
Specialist teaching staff
An outstanding team of teaching staff is Cricklade Prep’s greatest asset, chosen and developed to provide the best possible learning opportunities for our children. Each member of staff is highly experienced, and many have subject specialisms, so that even our youngest pupils learn from experts in their field.
Staff and pupils work within a curriculum that is broad and flexible, allowing for high quality education in the core academic subjects, and the opportunity to really extend learning into areas as diverse as Lego robotics, entrepreneurship and outer space.
Exceptional facilities
The facilities at Cricklade Manor Prep are exceptional for a school of its size. We have fully equipped science laboratories, a large sports hall and a swimming pool on site, as well as 8 acres of outdoor space, encompassing sports fields, play areas and an exciting forest school. All of these are used to their full potential by teaching staff who are really enthusiastic about their subjects. Find out more about Cricklade Manor Prep Facilities
Opportunities
Providing opportunities, within and beyond the curriculum, allows every child to discover whatever it is that will motivate and inspire them.
Beyond the core curriculum, we seek ways to expand experience and learning. from school trips and entrepreneurship and environmental programmes, to participating in Young Voices at the O2, to the yearly Science Spectacular, school productions and positions of responsibility, and dynamic after-school clubs.
We have outstanding science, art and music departments, bringing very high quality provision in each of these. Sport is a particular strength, and given plenty of time int he curriculum. Children take part in weekly competitive matches in a wide range of sports from Year 3. The school also hosts Cricklade Cricket Club, and Cricklade Rugby Club’s summer training. Fencing is available as an after-school club, and our fencers compete regularly at regional, national and international competitions.
Outstanding outcomes
The outcomes our children achieve speak for themselves. This year, many children gained places at grammar schools, including two to the highly competitive Pates school in Cheltenham. All children applying for independent senior school secured places.
We are incredibly proud of all our children achieve, academically, on the sports field and in the visual and performing arts, all of which has been recognised by future schools. Cheerful, resilient, creative and innovative, at Cricklade Manor they have also learned a set of skills that will support and nourish them as they move on to the next stage in their education.
Supporting the whole family
Cricklade Manor Prep is a community of children, parents and staff. Communication between school and parents is key, and we have a clear and effective system to keep parents up to date on children’s progress.
We understand the pressures of family life, particularly for people juggling work and parenthood. Families can take advantage of wrap-around care, from 7.30 am-6 pm, with up to three delicious, freshly cooked meals a day, and a choice of over 25 exciting after-school clubs for the children to enjoy. There are also holiday clubs
Our school bus serves large parts of the surrounding area, and can also pick up from and deliver back to key local employers, including Nationwide.
More affordable than you may think
Cricklade Manor Prep operates on the principle that exceptional education, with a broad range of opportunities and excellent outcomes, should not cost the earth.
We also run a scholarship programme for entry into Year 3 for particularly gifted children.
We would love to meet you and discuss any questions you may have on a personal tour of the school.

Every spring, parents brace themselves to discover which primary schools have been allocated to their children. The news will be a cause for celebration for some, and disappointment for others. Either way, it’s big news. There are few things, after all, likely to have as big an impact on your child’s young life as their first school and those early experiences of formal education. But have you considered all the options?
Private schools (also called independent and sometimes, confusingly, public schools) may not be on your radar. There are certainly plenty of parents within our group of schools who tell us that private education never crossed their minds until a chance conversation with a friend, concerns about their child’s progress or a last-minute decision to visit an Open Day led them to explore the idea, and ultimately decide that it was the right choice for them.
More affordable than you may think
A common misconception is that private schools are only for the very wealthy.
It’s true that the Etons and Harrows of this world sit well outside the budget of most of us, but there are plenty of schools that provide an exceptionally good education without charging exorbitant fees. Prices start at around £675 per month, and some schools also offer bursaries and scholarships.
Importantly, when it comes to schools, a low price doesn’t necessarily equate to low quality. It all depends what you are looking for. The most expensive independent private schools have lots of shiny facilities – Olympic-standard sports halls, professionally equipped theatres – costs that are passed on to parents by way of hefty school fees.
Remove those high-cost items from the offering, and there are still significant benefits that a private school can offer, at a much more affordable price. Smaller class sizes than in the state sector, a reliably strong standard of education with excellent teachers, broad and exciting opportunities within and beyond the curriculum, sport as an integral part of school life with lots of competitive fixtures, and room for the arts; all these are things that smaller private schools provide at a relatively low cost. With excellent outcomes for the pupils, lots of parents look at private schooling as an investment in their children’s futures.
Choice
If a private school is within your reach, the first benefit is choice. If your budget can accommodate it, and if space allows, the private school route puts you in control, and allows you to choose a school that you decide is right for your child. Few private prep schools have an entry exam, although they may assess your child to make sure that he or she will get the right level of support.
It is also worth remembering that private schools only do well if they are strong and competitive. The independent nature of schools sets the standard and provides added accountability.
Smaller classes and no combined year groups allow the individual to flourish
Whenever we ask our parents what made them choose one of our schools, the top reason is small class sizes. State schools typically have 30 children in a class, and in the smaller schools, that might also result in children across several year groups being taught by one teacher in one classroom.
The higher teacher-to-child ratio in private schools ensures that every child gets more time and attention. Private school classes are frequently half the size of their state school counterparts, making it far easier to tailor an education to the individual child, identifying strengths and weaknesses and adapting the learning accordingly. In the early years, it might result in something as fundamental as having enough time to hear everyone in the class read three times a week. As the children grow, teachers can provide increased support for those needing it and extra challenges to stretch the more gifted boys and girls.
It’s not just the teacher’s time that is more generously shared. Small classes give children more access to the best resources, such as computers, science equipment or musical instruments, or increased opportunities to play sport for the school or take on positions of responsibility. There is enough flexibility to focus on the children as people and not just pupils, with more room to develop camaraderie, good manners, compassion and resilience.
Facilities
Even without the big ticket items mentioned above, a private school usually provides lots of outdoor space, and frequently beautiful and inspirational surroundings, to nurture the spirit and fire learning. Private prep schools often have the sort of resources you would only find in a state secondary school, such as proper science laboratories or IT suites stocked with computers, 3D printers and Lego robotics. Along with sports pitches, there will be properly equipped performance spaces where children can build confidence in public speaking and drama, and with an increasing focus on outdoor learning, many schools have a dedicated Forest School area within their grounds.
Excellent teaching
Of course, private schools don’t have a monopoly on enthusiastic, talented and inspired teachers. However, they do give those same teachers better opportunities to deliver an outstanding education, and much more flexibility in how the curriculum is delivered, unencumbered by budget cuts and limited resources.
You are likely to find more subject experts, so that children will be taught science and modern foreign languages by a dedicated leads and sport by qualified coaches. As children approach the end of their time at prep school, they will be well prepared for any entry exams to independent or grammar senior schools they need to take.
Opportunities to find strengths, interests and passions from broad curricular and extra-curricular offering
Unlike state schools, independent schools are not bound by the National Curriculum. This gives head teachers the opportunity to broaden the offering, expand individualised learning and make education exciting and engaging with the creative curriculum.
Time will be found for all sorts of varied experiences to help prepare the children for the future, including entrepreneurship and leadership opportunities. There are also significantly more opportunities for sport, with high quality coaching, and regular matches with other schools. Swimming lessons are pretty standard fare in private schools, as well as less common sporting activities such as Judo and Fencing.
Beyond the classroom, there are other options that you would be unlikely to find in a primary school, including trips abroad, skiing holidays and sports tours.
This breadth of experience helps children develop a whole raft of qualities that will serve them well all their lives: confidence, resilience, initiative, perseverance, independence, adaptability and decision-making.
Convenience
When both parents work, which is often the case at schools in the Wishford group, childcare is a huge factor to consider. At most independent schools, the school day is a little longer, with wrap-around care, the option to have three hot meals a day and holiday camps on offer to make life easier for working parents. Because of the smaller numbers, school bus services can be flexible, with routes planned around the pupils.
Value for money!
This may sound counter-intuitive, but a private education should be a really good investment. Choosing a private prep school doesn’t commit you to a private senior school. Within the Wishford Group schools, between a third and half of pupils move to state secondary and grammar schools. The thorough grounding they have received in those crucial early years gives them a real advantage when they arrive at secondary school, full of confidence to put themselves forward and grasp new opportunities, and with an appetite for knowledge and a strong work ethic that make future learning easier, and will have an impact long after they leave school altogether.
Discover more at Cricklade Manor Prep
A perfect way for you to find out more about independent schools and the fantastic opportunities they offer to your child, is to visit one of our Open Days or arrange a personal tour. We look forward to meeting you then.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reception Stay and Play: A Morning of Fun and Learning for our September 2026 starters! - Cricklade Manor Prep School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
Cricklade Manor Prep opened its doors to welcome preschool children and their families for our special Reception Stay and Play event. Designed to help children transition smoothly into school life, this event was a fantastic opportunity for little learners (and their parents!) to experience a slice of the excitement that starting school brings.
With September 2026 on the horizon, we know how important it is for children to feel confident and happy as they begin their school journey. The Stay and Play event is just one of the ways we ensure every child feels at home from day one—and judging by all the smiles, it was a great success!
The morning kicked off with an energetic specialist sports lesson in our sports hall, led by two of our subject specialist teachers, Mrs. Davies and Mr Deane. Reception children at Cricklade Manor Prep are lucky enough to enjoy subject-specialist lessons from the start, and the Stay and Play was the perfect chance for our young visitors to get a taste of this. From balancing to bouncing, running to rolling, it was a joy to see the children getting stuck in, cheering each other on, and having so much fun.
Next, it was time to explore the magical world of the Reception classroom with Mrs O’Dell and Miss Flavell, the Reception teachers, and their Learning Support Assistant, Miss Blanford. Here, the children joined a cosy literacy circle time, that sparked their imaginations. They also had free rein to dive into the exciting activities the classroom has to offer. From dressing up in costumes in imaginative play, experimenting with hands-on learning stations, and even getting messy while exploring numbers and nature, there was never a dull moment.
Parents loved seeing their children’s eyes light up as they discovered all the engaging and creative ways we encourage learning through play. It was a wonderful chance for families to meet the staff and start building connections that will continue as their children join the Cricklade Manor Prep community.
As the morning drew to a close, it was time for a cheerful farewell with promises of
“See you in September!”
The smiles, laughter, and enthusiasm we saw throughout the day reminded us why we do what we do—to make the start of school a truly happy and exciting chapter for every child.
We’re already looking forward to welcoming this bright and eager group of learners to Reception in September 2026. Thank you to everyone who came along and made the event so special—we can’t wait for the adventures ahead!
Interested in discovering Cricklade Manor Prep? Join us for our Open Day on Friday, 6th February, and experience the vibrant atmosphere and nurturing environment that sets us apart.
Can’t make it? Contact us admissions@cricklademanor.com or phone 01793 750275 to arrange a personal visit and see what makes Cricklade Manor Prep the perfect place for your child’s education.
Discover the exceptional opportunities awaiting your child at Cricklade Manor Prep!

pageCache.text:
Home » Admissions » Open Days
Cricklade Manor Prep is a vibrant, ambitious, and nurturing school. Our educational journey begins in our Nursery, which warmly welcomes children from three months to five years, and continues through our Prep School for pupils aged five to eleven. Based around our beautiful historic manor house, our site blends tradition with exceptional modern facilities.
Although we’ve had our Open Day this term, we still warmly welcome families to book a personal tour. Click the button below to register your interest and our admissions team will be in touch to arrange your visit. We can’t wait to welcome you.
What to expect from an Open Day:
An Open Day is an opportunity to experience the warm, vibrant atmosphere of our school in action. During your visit, you will be taken on a personal tour by either one of our confident Year 6 pupils or a member of our Senior Leadership Team. This offers an authentic look at daily life across our countryside grounds, specialist classrooms, and outdoor learning spaces, allowing you to see our small class sizes and tailored teaching approach in action across both Nursery and Prep.
From our expansive sports fields and forest school, to our dedicated science labs and creative arts spaces, we provide a stimulating environment where children are encouraged to challenge themselves, discover new passions, and develop the confidence to succeed. As a result, our pupils leave us well-prepared for the future, equipped with an appetite to learn, an enthusiasm for future challenges, and the confidence to take the lead.
Discover what makes us unique:
Can’t make our Open Day? Not to worry!
If you are unable to attend our Open Morning or would prefer an individual visit, our Admissions Team would be delighted to arrange a private tour. Exploring our school during a typical school day allows you to see our inspiring, broad curriculum, meet our specialist subject teachers, and explore our eight-acre site located conveniently between Swindon and Cirencester. You will also learn about our excellent outcomes for pupils, our exciting extra-curricular club offering, our year-round Nursery set in a delightful walled garden, flexible wrap-around care, and our dedicated school bus service.
If you have any questions or would like to arrange a private tour, our Admissions Team would love to hear from you. Please contact our Registrar at admissions@cricklademanor.com or call 01793 750275
We were pleased with the result of our latest inspection by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (the independent schools equivalent to Ofsted). The inspectors praised many aspects of our school, but best of all, they awarded us a ‘Significant Strength’ for our Cricklade Pupil Development programme. You can read the full report here.
